note: A voice for the Nomads, checked against the Kenshi wiki (2026-11-12): human wanderers and animal herders, neutral, content to tend their animals; they call settled people 'Townie'; they roam the south-west (Stenn Desert, Border Zone, Shem, Okran's Gulf, Dreg) and the north-east (Hidden Forest, Northern Coast, Darkfinger, Sinkuun, the Great Desert, Heng, Grey Desert); their camps are free to anyone (rain shelter, campfire, bed); a pack beast carries their light; they trade goats, pack beasts, bonedogs and bulls; they coexist with the Dust Bandits and the Band of Bones and are friendly with the Western Hive and Empire peasants. (Vanilla already has them feed a starving traveller cooked vegetables, so no gift here.) Vanilla gives their squads no dialogue packages; the compiler reaches them through their characters' own packages with a 'my faction' check.

say: Keep walking, Townie. It's the only thing that works.
Towns are where the trouble keeps its money.
Water, then shade, then talk. In that order.
We were here before the walls. We'll be here after them.
You've road dust on you. Good. Means you're honest about it.
Wheels break out here. Feet mend.
Our fires are open to anyone. Just don't make us regret it.
Walk with the wind at your back.
Need an animal, Townie? Nobody survives the road on their own back.
A pack bull carries what you can't.
Pack beasts are slow. So is dying of thirst.
Bonedogs bite strangers. That's what you're paying for.
Feed them first, then yourself. They remember.
A bull that size could pull a wagon, if anyone out here still built them.
Mind the goats. They don't mind you.
Goats know when the weather turns. Watch them, not the sky.
Goats eat anything. So do we.
Lost three to beak things last season. The rest walked on.
The hivers out west trade fair. Fairer than most Townies.
Dust Bandits leave us be. We've nothing they'd bother carrying.
My father walked from Shem to Heng twice. Never got rich.
The Bones and us drink at the same well.
Settled folk count walls. We count wells.
A town is a road that gave up.
Old Empire farmers used to share their water with us.
Out here alone? Either you're brave or you've nowhere left.
If you're lost, the road's that way. If you're not, keep it that way.
Follow the pack beast's lamp if night catches you.
Townie. Sit by the fire a while?
Fire's going. Sit, if you've the time.
You look like you've walked far.
I could use the rest.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Water's in the skin. Talk if you like, or don't.
Rest. The road will still be there. It always is.
Sit close. The nights out here bite.
Any news from the road?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Beak things on the move near the coast.
The painted ones came further south this year. Keep your fires small up north.
Acid rain over the south-east again. Our goats knew a day early.
Saw a caravan's bones off the road. Somebody wanted what it carried more than they wanted the drivers.
Skimmers in the dunes at night. Don't sleep in the open, Townie.
Hivers out west are trading again. Fair prices, if you can stand the staring.
Bandits on the old road, waiting for anyone fat enough to rob. You're thin. You'll be fine.
Not tonight.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: The fire keeps. So does the road.
Suit yourself, Townie.
